steps.what: Look up current directions and visitor information
Provide directions suited to the visitors and check their understanding

tasks.design: Configure bookmarked destination and closure views in the site information tool {OTHER}. The guide still interprets the visitor's needs, checks what is happening on site and explains the directions in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful site notices and maps are spread over separate views.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing information tools can group maps and current notices without generating advice.
tasks.still_hard: A nominally open route may be unsuitable for this visitor or blocked now.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confusion, fatigue and mobility needs and adapt the explanation.

ambition.what: The guide keeps the same responsibility for helping visitors.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: grouped map and notice views can reduce repeated navigation, while live directions need local judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is a routine spoken visitor enquiry, with an actual map lookup; no enquiry log is assumed today.

OTHER means the site's visitor information and map tool. Site operations produces destination names, map locations, notice dates and closure status. The guide reads original notices where fields are missing; no clean live route feed is assumed.

Test existing bookmarks and native search first. The six units removed are repeated navigation within the twenty-unit lookup; reading and checking notices retain fourteen. Existing map runtime earns no saving.
Shares are illustrative task work, not measurements or the prompt's time-share prior.
unknowns: How often a guide actually needs a lookup rather than memory
Whether notices are current and centrally available
research_questions: Does a grouped view remove navigation while retaining checks of current conditions?

already_counted.description: Read current notices and explain the route

incremental.description: Repair obsolete shortcuts and check notice dates

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R94, gross6, upkeep1, net5. If closures require opening the original notice each time, lookup retains19 of20, so gross1 less upkeep1 gives0. No invented post-conversation record.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read current travel times, opening conditions and site restrictions
Compare travel routes against travel time and site opening windows
Select travel routes using local knowledge and inspect the calculated feasibility
Enter the selected travel route and stop details in the working itinerary
Save the working travel itinerary in its existing document location

tasks.design: Use existing {OTHER} site records and a native {SPREADSHEET} schedule check to eliminate manual sequence arithmetic. Reusable stop fields in {DOCS} shorten entry into the real working itinerary; the guide selects the route and checks every feasibility assumption.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site facts, scheduling arithmetic and itinerary entry sit in separate tools.
tasks.enabler_now: Simple window constraints and reusable stop fields are sufficient; no model or agent is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Queues, group stamina, local conditions and the value of a stop need experienced judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a route that will be enjoyable and workable for this particular group.

ambition.what: Compare an accessible alternative before choosing the walking route.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: opening-window checks and travel-time sums are deterministic when their inputs are explicit; selecting an appropriate tour still needs local judgement.

assumptions: Boundary ends at the guide's existing working itinerary, used to conduct the tour. No booking, supplier order or traveller distribution is included or promised.

Site operators produce opening windows, duration, location and access conditions; transport sources produce dated travel estimates. The guide reads and transcribes missing values within s1. Manual repair of formula inputs is funded in incremental upkeep.
This estimate applies where the guide currently compares sequences manually in a sheet. Native route checks already running earn no new saving; test those first.

s1 removes five units of repeated source navigation, retaining twenty of reading and input capture. s4 removes4.8 units of stop formatting and repeated text, retaining19.2 of route-specific entry and verification. The ordinary save is tiny and fully retained.
unknowns: How often a route has no reusable stop template
research_questions: Can the checker flag an opening-window conflict without losing source dates or accessibility caveats?

already_counted.description: Read and capture route facts, choose and verify the route, complete and save the working itinerary

incremental.description: Repair irregular inputs and maintain time-window formulas and stop templates

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R65.2 gross34.8 less upkeep4 gives30.8. For atypical sites with unstructured hours and no reusable stop text, source work retains24 of25, manual schedule reconstruction20 of25 and itinerary entry23 of24; other work stays26. R93, gross7 less upkeep4 gives3. No shared benefit-halving formula.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check the required supplies and equipment list for this departure
Assemble the required supplies and equipment
Check the assembled supplies and equipment for completeness and safe condition

tasks.design: Link the existing departure checklist directly to the relevant tour specification in {DOCS}. Physical assembly and condition checks remain with the guide.
tasks.previous_blocker: The guide has to locate the right equipment list among similar tour documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document links can remove that search without changing the actual safety checks.
tasks.still_hard: A checklist cannot establish that a device works or a supply is fit for use.
tasks.human_edge: Handle the equipment and spot missing or unsafe items.

ambition.what: The physical preparation duty stays the same.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: linked checklists can reduce document search but cannot replace handling and inspecting tour equipment.

assumptions: Boundary is pre-departure assembly and checking, not a new inspection report. No routine record is assumed unless the operator actually requires one.
The tour organiser maintains the existing tour id, equipment categories, quantities and checklist version in DOCS; the guide reads and resolves missing requirements in s1.
Three units of checklist search disappear from the ten-unit read; seven units of reading and matching requirements remain. Existing checklist display runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Whether each tour has an existing checklist
Whether physical preparation requires a separately maintained inspection record
research_questions: Does a direct link save any search for guides who already know the checklist?

already_counted.description: Read the actual checklist, assemble items and inspect condition

incremental.description: Fix checklist links when tour specifications change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R97 gross3 minus upkeep0.5 gives2.5. If this departure has an unusual equipment variant the lookup retains9.5 of10, leaving0.5 gross minus0.5 upkeep=0. Physical work retains90 throughout.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Welcome and register visitors before issuing equipment

steps.what: Greet visitors and explain the registration process
Establish visitors' identities and actual attendance against the booking
Register visitors in the existing visitor system
Check the exact visitors' badge entitlement and safety device suitability before issue
Issue the required identification badges or safety devices to the checked visitors

tasks.design: Configure booking-linked registration fields in the existing visitor tool {OTHER} so the guide stops retyping names and booking references. Identity, actual attendance and physical suitability checks stay human before badges or devices are handed out.
tasks.previous_blocker: Booking details are visible but repeatedly typed into visitor registration.
tasks.enabler_now: Native booking-linked forms can prefill existing fields while preserving the guide's attendance check.
tasks.still_hard: A booked name does not establish that the right person has arrived or that a device fits.
tasks.human_edge: Welcome people and ensure that the right visitor receives appropriate equipment.

ambition.what: The guide keeps visitor admission and equipment responsibilities.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: booking-linked visitor forms can avoid repeated typing, but identity and equipment suitability require real-world checks.

assumptions: OTHER means the operator's booking and visitor registration tool. Booking staff already produce booking id, visitor name, date and party size; the guide establishes attendance and corrections in s2. Missing or changed details are entered manually within retained s3 work.
Boundary is an actual visitor register used by site access staff plus physical badge or device issue. No new welcome log or follow-up report is assumed.

Native prefill removes twelve of thirty registration units; eighteen remain for attendance flags, corrections and checking the saved entry. The same-system save is negligible, fully retained within s3 and ungated.

s4 is the guide's real operational check before handing items to visitors, not approval of the guide's own registration. Any changed visitor, item, condition or entitlement voids it. No new supervisor is introduced.
If the native booking tool already fills the register, that runtime earns no new saving.
unknowns: Whether the current visitor register requires duplicate booking entry
Which fields are required for actual site access
research_questions: How much typing remains after native prefill when visitors change at arrival?

already_counted.description: Welcome and identify visitors, correct registration, check exact issue set and hand over equipment

incremental.description: Repair booking-field mappings and handle exceptional roster imports

approvals.approved_version: Exact visitor-item issue set checked in s4 with current entitlement and equipment condition

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R88 gross12 minus upkeep2 gives10. With paper bookings or late substitutions, registration retains27 of30 instead of18; other work retains70. Gross3 minus upkeep2 gives1. No saving assigned to a save or physical handover.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

reach: Help travel guides compare feasible excursion sequences
skills_to_grow: Check source dates and route constraints
role.ambitious_version: Offer a checked accessible route alternative without reducing attention to the group.
